title: The Processes: Controlling, Delivery, Stage Boundaries and Closing

header.html: Explain the purpose, objectives and context of the processes controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary and closing a project
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 5

html:
1Controlling a stage

Purpose: assign work, monitor it, deal with issues, report progress to the board, and take corrective action so the stage stays within tolerance.

Objectives include: work is authorized and agreed, progress is monitored, issues and risks are managed, and the board is kept informed.

Context: it is the project manager's day-to-day process in each delivery stage. It uses work packages, checkpoint reports and highlight reports.

2Managing product delivery

Purpose: control the link between the project manager and the team manager(s) by placing formal requirements on accepting, executing and delivering project work.

Objectives include: work is agreed (a work package accepted), delivered to the agreed quality, and progress reported back.

Context: it is the team manager's process; it receives work packages from the project manager and returns completed products.

3Managing a stage boundary

Purpose: enable the board to review the success of the current stage, approve the next stage plan, review the updated project plan and confirm continued business justification and acceptable risk.

Objectives include: the board has enough information, the business case and plans are updated, and lessons are captured.

Context: it occurs near the end of every stage except the last. Main outputs: the end stage report and the next stage plan (or an exception plan).

Exam tip

. Stage boundary = review this stage, plan the next, confirm the business case. No stage boundary at the end of the last stage: that is closing a project.

4Closing a project

Purpose: provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed, and recognize that the objectives in the PID have been achieved (or the project has nothing more to contribute).

Objectives include: verify the product is accepted, hand over to operations, review performance (end project report), record lessons, and plan follow-on actions (including benefits review).

Context: it is the final stage of the project, and can also be done early if the board decides to stop the project (a premature close).

Exam tip

. Controlling a stage is the project manager's process; managing product delivery is the team manager's. Stage boundary is not used at the end of the last stage.

Exam tip

. If the board stops a project early, the project is closed prematurely using the closing a project process.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which process assigns work to be done and monitors it day to day within a stage?

  • ADirecting a project
  • BClosing a project
  • CControlling a stage
  • DStarting up a project
Show the answer

Answer: C. The project manager controls the stage.

S2Which statements are CORRECT? (1) Managing product delivery links the project manager and the team manager. (2) Managing a stage boundary happens at the end of the final stage. (3) Closing a project confirms acceptance of the project product. (4) Managing a stage boundary is carried out by the team manager.

  • A2 and 4
  • B1 and 3
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: B. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

S3Identify the missing word. Managing a [ ? ] enables the board to approve the next stage plan.

  • AStage boundary
  • BWork package
  • CHighlight report
  • DProduct register
Show the answer

Answer: A. That is the stage boundary process.

S4Which process produces the end project report?

  • AControlling a stage
  • BClosing a project
  • CManaging product delivery
  • DStarting up a project
Show the answer

Answer: B. Closing a project produces the end project report.

S5A team manager receives a work package and returns the completed product. Which process is this?

  • ADirecting a project
  • BInitiating a project
  • CManaging a stage boundary
  • DManaging product delivery
Show the answer

Answer: D. That is managing product delivery.

S6The board decides to stop a project early. Which process is used?

  • AClosing a project (premature close)
  • BInitiating a project
  • CControlling a stage
  • DManaging product delivery
Show the answer

Answer: A. A premature close uses closing a project.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of controlling a stage?

Show the answer

Assign and monitor work, handle issues, report progress and keep the stage within tolerance.

R2Who works in managing product delivery?

Show the answer

The team manager(s), linked with the project manager.

R3When does managing a stage boundary occur?

Show the answer

Near the end of each stage except the last.

R4What does closing a project confirm?

Show the answer

Acceptance of the project product.

R5Name two outputs of managing a stage boundary.

Show the answer

The end stage report and the next stage plan.

R6What is a premature close?

Show the answer

Closing the project early because the board decides to stop it.

6Quick Reference Card

Process Purpose in a phrase
Controlling a stage assign, monitor, report, correct
Managing product delivery accept, execute, deliver work packages
Managing a stage boundary review stage, plan next, confirm business case
Closing a project confirm acceptance, hand over, lessons
